fits.v: yes, but the aperture is bigger than the deck
fits.why: The NC dash is believed to take a double-DIN unit. A single-DIN deck fits with a double-DIN cage and a half-height pocket or blanking plate — the standard way any 1-DIN radio goes into a 2-DIN hole.

aperture.why: Confirm on your car. If it is double-DIN you need the pocket; if single, you do not.

depth_mm.why: This is the number that decides whether the build fits, and it is the one no listing tells you. Measure from the back of the aperture to the nearest obstruction before you commit to a chassis depth.

fascia_adapter.v: search: “Mazda MX-5 NC double DIN fascia with 1-DIN pocket”
fascia_adapter.why: The pocket is the part that makes a 1-DIN deck look deliberate in a 2-DIN hole rather than lost in it.

harness.why: ⚠️ Cars with the Bose system are wired differently from the base system. Establish which you have before ordering.

aerial.why: The NC generally uses a fixed aerial rather than a powered mast.

swc.v: ⚠️ present on some trims — unlike the NA and NB
swc.why: This is the one car in this directory where the steering-wheel controls are worth checking for. If yours has them, they work through the same universal interface box and the deck's learning wizard; see docs/CONTROL.md. If not, skip it.

illumination.v: dash dimmer at the ISO A connector

ignition.v: switched live at the ISO A connector

same_as_other_generations: ISO 7736 and ISO 10487 via an adapter, as everywhere else
⚠️ NOT the same on steering-wheel controls: the NC may have them and the NA/NB do not
market_notes: Trim level matters more than market on the NC, because of the Bose option and the steering-wheel controls.
⚠️ The radio band plan follows where the car is driven, not where it was built. An import wants the plan of the country it is in now.
gotchas: The Bose system is an amplified system and does not behave like plain speakers on an ISO block. Establish what you have before cutting anything.
The deck is line-out only and has no amplifier. Plan for one, or accept that it will be quiet.
The deck has no aerial-power output. If the car has a powered or amplified aerial it needs 12 V from a switched source of your own.
A 1-DIN deck in a 2-DIN hole needs the pocket to look intentional.

factory_amp.v: ⚠️ Bose-equipped cars have one; base cars believed not
factory_amp.why: ⚠️ This matters more on the NC than any other car here. A Bose system is amplified and does NOT behave like plain speakers on an ISO block — establish which you have before buying an amplifier or cutting anything.

amp_space.v: the bottom half of the dash aperture, or the boot
amp_space.why: ✅ The NC is the best case in this document: a double-DIN hole means the amplifier can sit behind the fascia with the deck.

din_options.v: 2-DIN, which permits the one thing a single-DIN car cannot: **the deck in the top half and the amplifier board in the bottom half.** That is what a real head unit does — amp and front end in one box — and it is the only route in this project where the amp lives in the dash rather than under a seat. The alternative is deck + storage pocket.
